A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TAP, with matching methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TAP classification experiments, ablations, visualizations, and the appendix comparison of descriptions generated by different LLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TAP experiments and analyses in Tables 1–10 and Figures 3–4, including the appendix results.

M1.justification: The tree-generation procedure, visual expert tokens, vision-conditional pooling, training losses, regularization, and prediction fusion are unchanged. The new attribute inventories document existing inputs rather than establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 datasets for base-to-novel generalization, cross-dataset transfer, and 16-shot classification. Appendix A.5 lists attributes for existing datasets without introducing new evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Tables 1–3 and the MaPLe comparison in Table 9. Newly cited methods in the revised related work are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same class splits, 16-shot settings, ViT-B/16 backbone, metrics, training schedules, and hyperparameters. Expanded captions restate existing protocols, while the new attribute lists supply previously undisclosed details.

E4.justification: The ablations of tree structure, expert tokens, fusion weight, attribute count, pooling, and regularization remain unchanged. The GradCAM and attention examples and Appendix A.3 LLM robustness comparison were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experimental results are averaged over three runs. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain the same numerical results, and Figures 3–4 retain the same qualitative evidence. TAP's average harmonic mean remains 81.04, cross-dataset target accuracy 66.56, and 16-shot accuracy 83.37. The added attribute inventories document configurations rather than new evaluation findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–12, including the appendix regularization objectives, are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: structured attribute trees, expert tokens, vision-conditional pooling, and improved performance across the three evaluation settings. Their headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of attribute specialization and instance-dependent description selection remain unchanged. The conclusion retains the limitation that LLMs can generate identical descriptions for distinct fine-grained classes; the revised related work restates mechanisms already explained in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a TAP-specific code URL to the abstract and Appendix A.5 with explicit dataset attribute inventories. Tables 11–12 list ten datasets, omitting OxfordPets despite their 11-dataset captions. Existing implementation settings and generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 refines the positioning around structured knowledge generation and hierarchy exploitation, adding work such as graph-based captioning and hierarchical linguistic prompting. It removes the TransHP discussion and citation and adds several other references, while retaining TAP's central distinction from earlier approaches.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the two related-work paragraphs. v2 also adds acknowledgments and Appendix A.5, updates affiliation and corresponding-author information, and makes small wording corrections; the main methodological and experimental narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds attribute Tables 11–12, expands the captions of Figure 1 and Tables 1, 2, and 8, and adds conference headers with associated page reflow. The four figures and existing result-table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The TAP-specific code pointer and concrete attribute inventories improve reproducibility documentation, while expanded captions make comparisons more self-contained. These gains are limited: the inventories omit OxfordPets, and Section 2 adds molecular-screening citations to the CoOp generalization discussion without explaining their connection. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
